summary: Defines two YANG modules. The first is the initial version of the IANA-maintained module for Maximum Segment Identifier Depth types, for MPLS and SRv6. The second augments the IETF MPLS YANG model to support MPLS MSDs.

eli5.summary: Routers can only stack so many labels on a packet. This gives a standard form for writing down and managing that limit.

questions: yang model for maximum sid depth
what is the iana-msd-types yang module
what is node msd vs link msd
subtitle: Two YANG modules that let routers report how many segment labels they can handle, with types kept in step with an IANA registry.

tldr.problem: Routers can only push or process a limited number of segment identifiers (SIDs) on a packet, and there was no standard YANG way to type or read that Maximum SID Depth (MSD).
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines iana-msd-types, a module of MSD type identities that mirrors the IANA 'IGP MSD-Types' registry, and ietf-mpls-msd, which augments the MPLS base model with read-only node-msds and link-msds lists.
tldr.outcome: Management systems get a common, machine-readable way to read a node's MSD capabilities for the MPLS data plane, and the type list can be updated by IANA as the registry grows.

facts.label: Meaning of 0
facts.value: No ability to support a SID stack of any depth

today: RFC 9702 is a Proposed Standard published in January 2025, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It is the initial version of both modules; the iana-msd-types module is maintained by IANA from here on.

sections.title: Overview of the Two Modules
sections.content:
RFC 9702 defines two YANG modules (YANG is the data modeling language from RFC 7950). The first, iana-msd-types, defines identities for Maximum SID Depth (MSD) types, taken from the 'IGP MSD-Types' IANA registry. That registry covers both the MPLS and the Segment Routing over IPv6 (SRv6) data planes.

The second, ietf-mpls-msd, augments the IETF MPLS YANG model (RFC 8960), which in turn augments the routing RIB model (RFC 8349). It exposes operational state for MSDs on the MPLS data plane, as a list of Node MSDs and a list of Link MSDs. Both modules conform to the Network Management Datastore Architecture (RFC 8342).
sections.eli5: There are two rule sheets. One is a list of the kinds of limits a router can have. The other is a place on the router to read those limits.

sections.title: Design of the Model
sections.content:
IANA created the 'IGP MSD-Types' registry under the 'Interior Gateway Protocol (IGP) Parameters' registry group. The iana-msd-types module is IANA-maintained and will be updated if and when the registry changes.

On top of the base identity msd-base, the identity msd-base-mpls is the base for MSD types in the MPLS data plane, and msd-base-srh is the base for MSD types for the Segment Routing Header (SRH) in the IPv6 data plane.

As defined in RFC 8491, a Link MSD is the number of SIDs supported by a node's link, and a Node MSD is the smallest MSD supported by the node across all its links. The module defines lists of MSDs and their types for a node and for its links. These are read-only data nodes that expose a node's hardware capability.
sections.eli5: Each link on a router has its own limit, and the whole router's limit is the smallest of its links, like a chain that is only as strong as its weakest link.

sections.title: The MPLS MSD Data Tree
sections.content:
The tree has two augmentations, both read-only (config false). The first adds a node-msds container under the MPLS container, holding a node-msd list. The second adds a link-msds container under each MPLS interface, holding a link-msd list.

Each list entry is keyed by msd-type, an identityref based on msd-base-mpls, and carries an optional msd-value of type uint8. The value is in the range 0 to 255, and 0 represents the lack of ability to support a SID stack of any depth. For the same type, the Node MSD value is the smallest among the Link MSD values.
sections.eli5: Each entry is a label saying what kind of limit it is, plus a number. A zero means the router cannot take any stack at all.

sections.title: Keeping the Module in Sync with IANA
sections.content:
IANA added a 'Data Plane' column to the 'IGP MSD-Types' registry so the base identity for each type is unambiguous. IANA also added a note saying new values must not be added directly to the iana-msd-types module. They must be added to the registry, and the module is then updated.

When a new MSD type is added, a new identity statement must be added. Its name is the lowercase type name with spaces replaced by a hyphen. Its base is the base of the matching data plane, its description replicates the registry name, and its reference replicates the registry reference with the document title. A new data plane gets an identity named msd-base- plus the lowercase data plane name. Unassigned or reserved values do not appear in the module, and every update adds a new revision statement in front of the existing ones.

The RFC also registers the two XML namespace URIs and the two module names (iana-msd-types and ietf-mpls-msd) with prefixes iana-msd-types and mpls-msd.
sections.eli5: IANA keeps the master list. Whenever a new kind of limit is added there, the matching entry has to be added to the module too, so the two lists never disagree.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The modules are meant to be accessed through network management protocols such as NETCONF (RFC 6241) or RESTCONF (RFC 8040). Their mandatory-to-implement secure transports are SSH and TLS respectively, and the Network Configuration Access Control Model (RFC 8341) can restrict access.

Some readable nodes in ietf-mpls-msd may be sensitive in some networks, so read access to node-msds and link-msds should be controlled. The reason given is that exposing a node's maximum SID depth may help mount a Denial-of-Service attack, by sending the node packets it cannot process. The iana-msd-types module exposes no readable or writable data nodes, so it raises no additional issues.
sections.eli5: Telling strangers exactly how much a router can handle could help them overload it, so only trusted people should be allowed to look.
